title: Cron Expression Explainer
description: Explain a standard five-field cron expression in plain language and list the next run times. Supports lists, ranges and steps. Runs locally.
intro: Paste a minute-hour-day-month-weekday expression. The explainer names each field and estimates the next few matching times in your local timezone.
blurb: Turn a five-field cron expression into plain language and upcoming run times.
howItWorks: Enter five space-separated fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
Use * for any, commas for lists, hyphens for ranges and / for steps, such as */15 or 1-5.
Press Explain to see a field-by-field reading and the next matching local times.
examples: 0 0 1 * * means midnight on the first day of each month.

faq.q: Which cron dialect does this cover?
faq.a: Standard five-field cron used by Vixie cron and many schedulers. It does not parse seconds, years, or names such as JAN or MON.

faq.q: How are day-of-month and day-of-week combined?
faq.a: If both fields are restricted, a time matches when either field matches, which is the usual cron OR rule. If either field is *, only the other field is applied.

faq.q: Is the expression sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Parsing and the next-run search happen in your browser. Results use your device timezone.
